title: KLM Offloaded A Passenger Rather Than Use The Blocked Seat We Offered
summary: I recently flew KLM from Amsterdam to Barcelona, and a passenger was taken off our full flight even though my wife and I offered him the empty seat between us. The crew followed a rule exactly, and as far as I can tell, nobody got anything out of it. Intra-European business class basics Business class
content: I recently flew KLM from Amsterdam to Barcelona, and a passenger was taken off our full flight even though my wife and I offered him the empty seat between us. The crew followed a rule exactly, and as far as I can tell, nobody got anything out of it. Intra-European business class basics Business class inside Europe is basically a regular economy seat with the middle seat blocked. On some planes the middle seat is physically blocked with a small table. On this flight it was just empty, blocked online so nobody could book it, but technically a regular seat anyone could sit in. I was on KL1519 on 2 September, in row 2 with my wife, with that empty middle seat between us. Same seat on two boarding passes After the doors closed, it turned out that two passengers had boarding passes for the same seat. Whoever got there first sat down. The other one was a fairly young guy, and now he had nowhere to sit. The flight was completely full, there wasn’t a single free seat in economy. I heard the crew apologizing to him and saying they would have to take him off the plane and put him on the next flight. I knew this would take a while, because the doors were already closed and he had boarded. Getting him off meant opening the doors again, and maybe taking his bag off too. Once on another flight someone got off and everyone had to hold up their bags. And I felt sorry for the guy. Maybe he was in a hurry to get somewhere, and none of this was his fault. The airline gave two people boarding passes for one seat, and he was already on board. We offered our blocked middle seat So I asked my wife if she minded giving up the empty seat between us. The flight is only about two hours. She was fine with it, so I went to the crew and offered it. The crew was very grateful, but said seating someone there was against the rules and they couldn’t decide it themselves, they had to check with someone. That took about 10 minutes. Then they came back, thanked me again, and said that unfortunately it wasn’t possible under the rules. So they opened the doors and offloaded the guy, I hope they rebooked him on the next one. In the end we pushed back about 40 minutes late and landed in Barcelona about half an hour late. After landing I think even the captain came over, shook my hand and thanked me. What I don’t get about this rule As I understand it, the middle seat is blocked to give the business class passengers more space. In this case that was us, and we were the ones offering to give that space up. We didn’t need the space, and we’d have put up with one more person in the row for two hours. Bottom line On a completely full KLM flight, two passengers got boarding passes for the same seat. My wife and I offered the empty blocked seat between us in business, so he wouldn’t have to get off. The crew checked with someone, the answer was no, and he was offloaded anyway, and we left about 40 minutes late. I get that the crew couldn’t make this call themselves. Still, we didn’t need that seat at all. Is there a good reason for this rule that I’m missing?

title: Why JetBlue Is My Favorite Way To Fly Economy Across The Atlantic
summary: After dozens of Atlantic crossings, JetBlue's economy cabin stands out for its fresh meals, free fast Wi-Fi, comfy A321LR seats and surprising extras like a Snooze Kit.
content: I’ve flown back and forth across the Atlantic dozens of times in all cabins, including many times in economy. JetBlue definitely stands out as being my favorite, and dare I say it, the most premium of all the transatlantic economy flights I’ve experienced. My most recent trip was from Europe to Boston (BOS) for the opening of JetBlue’s newest BlueHouse location. The airline covered my flights for the event, but had no input in this article. I’d like to share some of the reasons that JetBlue’s transatlantic experience impressed me so much. JetBlue serves up excellent food and drink Economy class meals can seem like quite the downgrade should one be accustomed to the elevated fare at the pointy end of the plane. JetBlue currently partners with NYC-based Dig Inn for its transatlantic economy-class meals, and they’re far better than average. They also offer products from a range of interesting brands, rather than just your classic soda labels. I loved this Bubly sparkling blackberry-flavored water Here’s an example of the drinks menu on my flight from Amsterdam to Boston. Alcohol is also complimentary for eligible passengers When seated in the Even More Space section on the flight from Amsterdam (AMS) to Boston (BOS), I was even offered a pre-meal snack of cookies. I’d take this over a bowl of warm nuts in business class any day… Calories in the air don’t count Meals are served in these stylish, reusable, matte-black sealed containers. I’d love to see more airlines do more to reduce their waste like this. Remove lids for a treat I was very happy with my choice of chicken pesto pasta salad as the main course, accompanied by sides of beet and carrot slaw and snap peas with feta. The fresh, flavorful, yet cold dishes were far better than many of the reheated slop I’ve been served in economy before. Yum yum yum I was equally impressed by the breakfast I had on the morning departure back from Boston to London Heathrow (LHR). I went for the Bubly sparkling water again, as I avoid coffee on a plane unless it’s served as espresso. The stuff they pour out of those vats is pretty much just glorified dirty water. A stellar in-flight breakfast As far as pre-landing light meals go, this pizza thing was pretty good, too. It tasted more like a pizza than it looked In addition to the main meal and pre-landing light bite, JetBlue keeps a well-stocked pantry at the back of the Airbus A321LR. I’m a sucker for those cheddar Goldfish JetBlue invested in great tech, including fast free Wi-Fi for all JetBlue has been offering fast, free, in-flight Wi-Fi for as long as I can remember. The same cannot be said for some full-service carriers, which still can’t guarantee a reliable, fast, and free connection on their transatlantic flights. They’ve also added some fun tech features, like the ability to choose the elements for the main meal service via the IFE screen, even in economy. I think it has a more premium feel than being asked “chicken or beef?” The crew asked several times for us to make our choice ASAP I’m not a frequent JetBlue flyer, so I couldn’t really make the most of the fun personalization features, such as the option to continue watching the movie where you left off on your last flight. Personalization is everything in today’s travel world I got amenities on a day flight in economy Being given anything more than the standard pillow and blanket in economy is a rare bonus. It had been so long since my last JetBlue flight in economy that I’d forgotten about the complimentary Snooze Kit. Anything more than a blanket and pillow in economy is rare I prefer to use my AirPods to earplugs, but I did make good use of the eye mask for a mid-flight nap. Normalize complimentary eye masks in economy The Airbus A321LR is a comfy ride I’ve flown over my fair share of narrow bodies on long-haul flights, and I genuinely don’t know why such a fuss is made about them being terrible. JetBlue’s version of the aircraft has comfy seats, with standard Core (economy) seats having 32 inches of pitch. Another common complaint I hear is that there are fewer toilets. For a plane with far fewer passengers (only 114 in economy), fewer toilets kind of makes sense. I didn’t once find myself waiting in line to use the bathroom on either flight. For what it’s worth, there are two lavatories for 114 economy passengers, so that’s one lavatory per 57 passengers. That’s a little lower than the industry standard, but not by much. For example, American’s standard 787-9s have five lavatories for 255 economy seats, so that’s a ratio of one lavatory per 51 passengers. Bottom line If you’ve only got the budget or the points for economy for your next trip to Europe, I couldn’t recommend JetBlue more. They now fly to eight cities in Europe, the planes are comfortable and modern, and the in-flight food and beverage is top of the game for economy. What do you make of JetBlue’s transatlantic economy offering?

title: LATAM Refused My Refund Within 24 Hours, And The Reason Makes No Sense
summary: A booking mix-up with a UK credit card left me unable to cancel a LATAM ticket within the 24-hour cooling-off period, despite calling on time.
content: Over the weekend, I booked an expensive ticket for my dad, brother, and me, from Buenos Aires (EZE) to Santiago (SCL), only to come across a better deal after I’d booked. I called customer service to cancel within the 24-hour cooling-off period, but was refused a refund for the most convoluted and unnecessary reason. LATAM is the airline I’ve flown with the second most in my life after British Airways, my old home airline. It’s an airline I look forward to flying with for several reasons. However, this recent booking experience has uncovered a gaping hole in its customer service, which in the air I’ve always found to be excellent. LATAM’s Brazilian website doesn’t accept UK cards for payment This whole situation could have been avoided if I’d been able to pay with my UK credit card on LATAM’s Brazilian website. The Brazilian site has no issue when entering UK credit card details. It let me enter my UK card details and everything However, the default setting for postcodes (ZIP codes) is numerical-only because, as in the US, Brazil’s postcodes consist only of numbers. In the UK, they’re made up of letters and numbers, so I couldn’t add the postcode that my credit card is registered to. The error says, “The ZIP code can only contain numbers” I tried using only the numbers of my postcode (the one in the example above is random), but the site returned an error, saying it failed to connect to my bank. My guess would be this wouldn’t be a problem for US credit cards, given that ZIP codes consist only of numbers too. This time the error said, “We couldn’t connect to your bank” I remember this happening previously, but I never had an issue with a booking that I couldn’t change online. Ideally, I would have paid with a Brazilian bank account or credit card, but I’m still working through the immigration bureaucracy required to open one. Brazilian customer service wouldn’t deal with my call First of all, I tried to cancel by logging into my LATAM Pass account, but was redirected to the contact center. This is when I realized how much of an obstacle my booking via the UK website would be. After being put on hold 3 times for what seemed like forever, the agent I spoke with at LATAM’s Brazilian call center told me there was nothing she could do to help me. She explained the only way I’d get a refund was to call the UK call center, since I’d paid in GBP on the UK website. I called just before the cut-off of the 24-hour cooling-off period, so by then I had exceeded it. I had only left it so close to the cooling-off period because I was researching the trip again the following day and found a better deal; otherwise, I wouldn’t have wanted to cancel. This was the first negative experience I’ve had with LATAM If I had called sooner and had more time, I could have asked someone in the UK to call for me, as my Brazilian phone number can’t make outgoing international calls. I did top up my UK SIM Card with 20 GBP, but at a charge of 2 GBP per minute, the call disconnected after 10 minutes on hold with no answer. Irrespective of whether I could have found an easier way to contact the UK call center, I can’t help but feel that my issue should have been resolved there and then over the phone by the Brazilian call center agent. After all, I booked directly through the airline’s website, and then called the airline directly to cancel. It makes no logical sense! Bottom line Because of a stupidly convoluted system, I’m stuck with a LATAM ticket that I can no longer cancel, even though I called customer service within the 24-hour cooling-off period. It’s not the end of the world, as we can still take the flights we’d originally booked, but it’s so frustrating to be put in a situation like this in 2026 because of such an archaic technicality. I’m still a big fan of LATAM itself, and will continue to fly it, at least until my Platinum status runs out next year. What’s the most frustrating post-sale customer service experience you’ve had?

title: Malaysia Airlines Orders Up To 16 Boeing 787-10s, Deliveries Start 2032
summary: Malaysia Airlines has placed its first-ever Dreamliner order: 10 firm Boeing 787-10s plus six options, with deliveries from 2032 to 2035. Here's how it fits the fleet.
content: Malaysia Airlines has just placed a new aircraft order , as the airline will be adding a new wide body aircraft type to its fleet. This seems logical enough, even if the carrier’s long haul fleet seems rather diversified at this point. Malaysia Airlines will add largest Dreamliner to fleet Malaysia Airlines has placed its first-ever Dreamliner order, as the airline will be taking delivery of up to 16 Boeing 787-10s. This includes a firm order for 10 jets, plus options for six more, with deliveries expected between 2032 and 2035. For context, the 787-10 is the largest variant of the Dreamliner. While it has the least range of any 787 variant, the per-seat economics are great, given how it’s “stretched.” While some airlines have started to use the 787-10 for high capacity regional routes, Malaysia Airlines is taking a different approach. The oneworld carrier intends to use these planes to support its long haul fleet modernization and international expansion, including routes to Europe, along with destinations throughout Asia-Pacific. The airline points out how long haul demand to and from Southeast Asia has increased by more than 50% over the past decade. Here’s how Malaysia Airlines Group CEO Nasaruddin Bakar describes this: “The acquisition of the 787 Dreamliner represents a strategic investment in the future of Malaysia Aviation Group. As we look ahead to the next phase of growth, these aircraft will strengthen our ability to serve key international markets with greater capacity, efficiency and flexibility, while delivering the elevated travel experience our customers expect. Beyond fleet renewal, this investment reinforces our commitment to maintaining a modern, competitive airline that supports Malaysia’s connectivity and global aspirations.” Malaysia Airlines will fly the Boeing 787-10 How the Dreamliner fits into Malaysia Airlines’ fleet For context, Malaysia Airlines currently has a fleet of just over 90 aircraft, with another 75 aircraft on firm order. As it stands, Malaysia Airlines has: 27 Airbus A330s, including three A330-200s, 13 A330-300s, and 11 A330-900neos Seven Airbus A350-900s 57 Boeing 737s, including 38 737-800s and 19 737 MAX 8s Now the airline has the following planes on firm order: 29 Airbus A330-900neos 36 Boeing 737 MAXs, including 24 737 MAX 8s and 12 737 MAX 10s 10 Boeing 787-10s A few things stand out here. First of all, it’s cool to see Malaysia Airlines growing again, after a rather rough… what, nearly 15 years? At this point the airline has enough planes on order to both replace its previous generation fleet, and expand. I’d expect the 16 A330ceos will be retired at some point in the coming years, and more than replaced by the A330neos that remain on order. Furthermore, the 737-800s will all be replaced by the 737 MAXs. The 787-10 is an incredible plane in terms of economics, especially as Boeing has been able to make incremental range improvements, turning it into a true long haul aircraft. At the same time, I can’t help but feel like it’s unusual how the airline has just seven A350s, with no more on order, and is now switching to the 787 for fleet renewal. Admittedly the A350 was ordered back in the day under a completely different management team, which also at one point thought the A380 was a good fit for the airline. So I am curious how the carrier’s fleet evolves. Will the seven A350s stick around, or will they eventually just be replaced by 787-10s? Even with airspace restrictions and headwinds, it seems like all of Malaysia Airlines’ routes should be within range for the 787-10, though admittedly London (LHR) might be on the cusp, depending on how airspace closures evolve, how dense of a configuration the airline selects, etc. The big challenge with the airline industry is that it’s never static, and decisions aren’t made in a vacuum. One management team makes one decision, and then a management team later on can’t just undo what the other management team did, without it being costly. So I get that they’re doing what they can… Malaysia Airlines will have three types of wide body planes Bottom line Malaysia Airlines is the newest customer for the Boeing 787, as the airline has ordered up to 16 787-10s, including 10 firm orders and six options. The airline plans to use this for a long haul expansion to Europe, as well as for flights in Asia-Pacific. It’s cool to see Malaysia Airlines continuing to grow, as the carrier has quite the order book at this point. I am curious if the airline keeps around the seven A350s in the long run, or how the airline manages its three wide body aircraft types. What do you make of Malaysia Airlines’ Boeing 787-10 order?

Admittedly the A350 was ordered back in the day under a completely different management team, which also at one point thought the A380 was a good fit for the airline. So I am curious how the carrier’s fleet evolves. Will the seven A350s stick around, or will they eventually just be replaced by 787-10s? Even with airspace restrictions and headwinds, it seems like all of Malaysia Airlines’ routes should be within range for the 787-10, though admittedly London (LHR) might be on the cusp, depending on how airspace closures evolve, how dense of a configuration the airline selects, etc. The big challenge with the airline industry is that it’s never static, and decisions aren’t made in a vacuum. One management team makes one decision, and then a management team later on can’t just undo what the other management team did, without it being costly. So I get that they’re doing what they can… Malaysia Airlines will have three types of wide body planes Bottom line Malaysia Airlines is the newest customer for the Boeing 787, as the airline has ordered up to 16 787-10s, including 10 firm orders and six options. The airline plans to use this for a long haul expansion to Europe, as well as for flights in Asia-Pacific. It’s cool to see Malaysia Airlines continuing to grow, as the carrier has quite the order book at this point. I am curious if the airline keeps around the seven A350s in the long run, or how the airline manages its three wide body aircraft types. What do you make of Malaysia Airlines’ Boeing 787-10 order?

title: Marriott Bonvoy Elite Status Soft Landings For 2027: Drop Only One Tier
summary: Marriott Bonvoy has confirmed its status soft landing policy for 2027: members who miss requalification in 2026 will drop at most one elite tier, matching its long-standing approach.
content: Marriott Bonvoy has just revealed its status soft landing policy for the next membership year, and it’s good news (well, at least for those who don’t requalify for their current status tier). Marriott Bonvoy’s 2027 status soft landing policy Marriott Bonvoy has just revealed its status soft landing policy for the 2027 status year, for situations where someone doesn’t qualify for a particular elite tier based on their activity in 2026. Specifically, elite members who don’t achieve the published criteria to maintain their status will only drop down at most one elite tier. In other words, Ambassador Elites will at most drop to Titanium Elite, Titanium Elites will at most drop to Platinum Elite, Platinum Elites will at most drop to Gold Elite, and Gold Elites will drop at most to Silver Elite. For what it’s worth, this policy matches Marriott’s historical approach to status soft landings. Before Marriott and Starwood merged, back when Marriott’s loyalty program was named Marriott Rewards, Marriott consistently had a status soft landing policy. With this, Marriott Rewards members never dropped more than one elite tier per year, regardless of their activity. That policy has continued since the new program was formed, including for the next year. However, there’s no guarantee this will continue to be the policy in the future. For those curious, the status offered as part of the soft landing also does count toward lifetime elite status . So if you’re downgraded from Titanium to Platinum based on a soft landing, that year of Platinum will add to your total. Marriott Bonvoy is offering status soft landings this year Status soft landings make a lot of sense During the pandemic, we saw airline and hotel loyalty programs largely extend elite status several times. This made sense, given the extent to which business travel decreased for many. However, with the huge increase in leisure travel and all the new ways to earn elite status , we’ve seen elite ranks swell. Personally I think the concept of a status soft landing makes a lot of sense. After all, sometimes life conditions change for people, and in many cases those changes are just temporary. If you drop from top tier status to no status, you don’t really have much of an incentive to stay loyal to that hotel group when your travel picks up again. By offering a soft landing, loyalty programs can try to build more of a long term relationship with members, and that’s a positive. We also see some programs allow members to pause their status for a year or extend status as a one-time exception based on life circumstances, and I think that’s a great policy as well. Marriott has long been generous with soft landings Bottom line Marriott Bonvoy has a generous status soft landing policy for 2027, for those who don’t requalify for status in 2026. If you didn’t requalify for your current status tier with Marriott Bonvoy in 2026, you can expect that you’ll be downgraded at most one status level. What do you make of Marriott Bonvoy’s soft landing policy for status?

title: SkyWest Pilots Do The Right Thing At SFO, Then Get Snapped At By ATC
summary: A SkyWest crew held short at SFO when a United pilot never read back instructions, then got a frosty response from the ground controller. Here's what was said.
content: With the number of close calls we see at airports nowadays, it’s great to see when pilots or air traffic controllers go above and beyond to be observant, and exhibit good situational awareness. So along those lines, here’s a case of a pilot paying close attention to ensure everyone’s safety, and then an air traffic controller being frustrated by that… SkyWest pilot’s situational awareness not well received YouTube channel You can see ATC has the air traffic control audio and a visualization of an interaction that happened shortly before noon on November 21, 2026, at San Francisco International Airport (SFO). In this interaction, a SkyWest Embraer E175 operating on behalf of American Eagle had just landed on runway 28L, after flying from Los Angeles (LAX). The pilots were switched to the ground frequency, and that’s when things quickly went downhill: The SkyWest pilots were instructed to taxi via A to the ramp, behind a KLM Boeing 787, and those instructions were read back correctly A United Boeing 737 was then instructed to give way to the SkyWest plane, but the United pilots never read back those instructions; as a result, the SkyWest pilots held short of the taxiway the United jet was on, since they weren’t sure if the pilots had heard those instructions Only several seconds lapsed here, and then the air traffic controller gave the United pilots instructions to “I guess just continue,” rather than giving way, since the SkyWest pilots were holding short of the taxiway The air traffic controller then asked if the SkyWest pilots were on frequency, and the SkyWest pilot said “yeah, I’m coming, he never read it back, we waited for him” The air traffic controller then responded that “if you’re not gonna go when I ask you to, even if you think there’s a problem, just let me know so that I can plan accordingly” The SkyWest pilots then continued their taxi, and when they got to the gate, the conversation continued: The SkyWest pilot said “ground, SkyWest 6316, can I get a number?” The phone number was given, and the SkyWest pilot responded “appreciate it, we’ll chat soon” The air traffic controller then snapped back “oh, you’ll be chatting to someone else, I’ll be gone” The SkyWest pilot then responded “perfect, hey, we’re not stepping on their read back and we’re not pulling out when they’re not pulling down, so please yell at them, not us” The air traffic controller then responded “I’m not yelling at anybody, I’m just keeping everyone apprised of everything, this conversation could be had off frequency” The SkyWest pilot then responded “well not if you’re not gonna have it with me, so we’ll see you on the phone” Kudos to the SkyWest pilots for their professionalism When you screw up, I suppose it’s human nature to get a bit defensive, and I think that’s exactly what happened here. Credit to the SkyWest pilots for their situational awareness here. They were instructed to taxi in front of another plane, and another plane was instructed to give way to them, but never read back those instructions. The air traffic controller absolutely should have caught that, and as a pilot, they 100% did the correct thing by noticing the lack of a read back, and erring on the side of caution. This isn’t just some theoretical risk, but ground collisions are the most common kinds of accidents involving commercial aircraft. Could the SkyWest pilots have said “we’re holding short because the other plane didn’t read back instructions?” Sure, but it seems like the time gap here was a matter of seconds, and they didn’t want to step on the radio calls of another pilot, in case they were going to read back. What I think is really unprofessional is how the air traffic controller then responded to this: It was professional how the SkyWest pilots wanted to discuss this off frequency, and asked for a phone number The air traffic controller was then dismissive in how she said “oh, you’ll be chatting to someone else,” as if she couldn’t care less about this Then when the SkyWest pilot briefly mentioned the issue “this conversation could be had off frequency,” literally right after saying they’ll be chatting with someone else Bottom line The pilots of a SkyWest flight decided to hold short of a taxiway after they observed the plane that was supposed to give way to them not reading back the correct instructions. That was absolutely the right move, and the air traffic controller should’ve caught that. When the pilots explained why they held short, the air traffic controller didn’t respond particularly well. Then when they asked for a phone number, she said the pilots would be talking to someone else, and she clearly wasn’t having it. But then she was also mad when the pilot explained very briefly what was going on, saying the conversation should happen off frequency… a conversation she wasn’t willing to have! This is a clear situation where you have two very professional pilots, and one very unprofessional air traffic controller. What do you make of this SFO ATC interaction?

title: Chase Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card Review: Are The Benefits Worth The Fee?
summary: The Aeroplan Credit Card offers up to 115,000 bonus points, a $195 annual fee, elite status, and a flexible Pay Yourself Back feature. Here's how it works.
content: The Chase Air Canada Aeroplan® Credit Card is one of the most compelling co-branded airline credit cards out there. I’m a huge fan of the Air Canada Aeroplan program — even if you have no connection to Air Canada or Aeroplan, the program is fantastic for partner redemptions, and this card is worth being aware of. And if you do fly Air Canada with any frequency, the perks for travel on the airline are strong. So this post is my in-depth Air Canada Aeroplan Card review. Let’s go over all the details, and discuss if the card is worth it. Link: Learn more about the Chase Air Canada Aeroplan® Credit Card Aeroplan Credit Card summary & key details for November 2026 Before I review the Air Canada Aeroplan Card benefits in detail, here’s a high-level look at everything you need to know about the card: Air Canada Aeroplan Card annual fee: $195 Air Canada Aeroplan Card welcome offer: Limited Time Offer: Earn up to 80,000 bonus points. Earn 60,000 bonus points after you spend $3,000 on purchases in the first 3 months your account is open. Plus, up to 20,000 more bonus points by earning 50% more bonus points per $1 spent on purchases that normally earn 1 bonus point in the first 2 months from account opening. Air Canada Aeroplan Card earning rate: Earn up to 5X total points for each dollar spent on Air Canada. Earn 3X points on travel purchases. Earn 2X points for each dollar spent at grocery stores, on dining at restaurants, and at gas stations. Earn 1X point for each dollar spent on all other purchases. Air Canada Aeroplan Card foreign transaction fee: $0 Air Canada Aeroplan Card benefits: Up to $100 in Air Canada statement credits (delivered as up to two $50 credits semi-annually), and save 15% on eligible Air Canada flight redemptions as a cardmember Air Canada Aeroplan elite status benefits: Complimentary Aeroplan 25K status, 5,000 automatic Status Qualifying Credits per calendar year, 10,000 SQCs once you spend $25K in a calendar year and an additional 10,000 SQCs after spending $50K in a calendar year, get Aeroplan 35K status after spending $75,000 on the card in a calendar year Here are my thoughts on the Air Canada Aeroplan Card’s biggest pros and cons: Chase Aeroplan Card pros Chase Aeroplan Card cons Complimentary Aeroplan 25K elite status and the ability to earn higher status through spending No lounge access benefit Strong bonus spending categories Non-Aeroplan loyalists may be better off earning transferable points Great spending-based incentives like reward vouchers Air Canada Aeroplan Card welcome bonus, eligibility, & fees If you’re thinking about applying for the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card , you’re probably most interested in the welcome bonus it’s currently offering, along with its annual fee and general eligibility rules for getting the card. So let’s get into those details. Aeroplan Card welcome bonus The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card currently has the following welcome bonus: Limited Time Offer: Earn up to 80,000 bonus points. Earn 60,000 bonus points after you spend $3,000 on purchases in the first 3 months your account is open. Plus, up to 20,000 more bonus points by earning 50% more bonus points per $1 spent on purchases that normally earn 1 bonus point in the first 2 months from account opening.. Based on my latest miles & points valuations , I consider Aeroplan points to be worth 1.4 cents each. That means the 80,000 points are worth $1,120 to me. However, even if you have a different valuation of these points than I do, you can at least use the “Pay Yourself Back” feature to redeem these points for 1.25 cents each toward a travel purchase, so that’s a pretty high “cash out” value. Redeem Aeroplan points for Lufthansa business class Aeroplan Card application rules & restrictions The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card is issued by Chase, and has pretty standard application restrictions: Chase’s normal credit card application rules apply, including the 5/24 rule , whereby you’ll generally get denied for Chase cards if you’ve opened five or more credit cards in the last 24 months You’re eligible for the bonus on this card as long as you don’t currently have this card, and haven’t received a bonus on this card in the past 24 months; in other words, eligibility is unrelated to having received a bonus on any other Chase card While Chase doesn’t have a public credit score requirement for the Air Canada Aeroplan Card, you’ll have the best chances of approval if your score is in the good range or higher. That roughly translates to a minimum score of 670. However, people have been approved with lower scores and rejected with higher scores, as it’s one of only many factors that determine card eligibility. Aeroplan Credit Card annual fee & authorized user fee The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card has a $195 annual fee. There’s no cost to add authorized users to the card, and their spending will count toward your points balance and any spending thresholds. Aeroplan Card no foreign transaction fees The Air Canada Aeroplan Card has no foreign transaction fees, so it’s a great card to use globally , and possibly even earn bonus rewards on your spending depending on what you’re using the card for. Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card rewards structure The Air Canada Aeroplan Card has a well rounded rewards structure, among the most interesting you’ll find on any airline credit cards. This isn’t just about the number of points that you earn, but also about the additional rewards for spending. Specifically, the Aeroplan Card offers the following: Earn up to 5x total points for each dollar spent on Air Canada (3x points from the card and 2x through the Aeroplan 25K status you get as a cardholder) — an excellent 7% return on spending using my valuation of Aeroplan points Earn 3x points on travel purchases — a 4.2% return on spending Earn 2x points per dollar spent at grocery stores, on dining at restaurants, and at gas stations — a 2.8% return on spending (through December 31, 2026, eligible purchases at grocery stores and dining at restaurants will earn 3x points per dollar spent) Those are some excellent bonus categories. For what it’s worth, the card offers 1x Aeroplan points on all other purchases, so there are better cards for everyday spending . Earn 3x points on travel purchases with the Aeroplan Card How to redeem Aeroplan points for best value There’s a lot to love about Air Canada Aeroplan points , even if you don’t usually fly Air Canada or travel to Canada. Among other things: Aeroplan has more airline partners than any other airline loyalty program in the world; not only can you book travel on all Star Alliance partners, but you can also redeem on a variety of other partners Aeroplan lets you add a stopover of up to 45 days on a one-way award for just 5,000 points, which is a great way to visit multiple destinations on the same trip Aeroplan doesn’t have fuel surcharges on award redemptions Aeroplan has reasonable award redemption rates , with a unique zone and distance based award chart I redeem miles through Aeroplan all the time, and consistently get great value. Booking award flights on Air Canada itself rather than other partners isn’t always the best deal, though, especially if you’re booking during a peak travel time, since Air Canada awards use dynamic pricing. Redeem Aeroplan points for Gulf Air business class Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card elite status benefits The Air Canada Aeroplan Card gives cardmembers plenty of opportunities to earn elite status with Air Canada Aeroplan. You get some status outright just for being a cardmember, and you can earn further status with spending. Automatic Aeroplan 25K status for new cardmembers Those who are approved for the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card receive Aeroplan 25K status. This is valid for as long as your account is open. Aeroplan Elite 25K is Air Canada’s entry level status, and includes travel perks with Air Canada, including: Priority check-in Priority boarding Five eUpgrade credits Two complimentary checked bags on Air Canada flights 2x elite points multiplier on Air Canada and Star Alliance partners booked through Air Canada Star Alliance Silver status Avis Preferred Plus status Potentially receive upgrades as an Aeroplan elite member 5,000 annual Status Qualifying Credits Each year, those with the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card also receive 5,000 Status Qualifying Credits (SQCs) to help work toward the next level of Aeroplan status. This is automatic, but as I’ll cover below, you can stack additional credits on top through hitting certain spending thresholds in the calendar year. For those curious, below are the Aeroplan elite requirements. Aeroplan status tier SQC required for status Star Alliance elite tier Aeroplan 25K 25,000 Silver Aeroplan 35K 35,000 Silver Aeroplan 50K 50,000 Gold Aeroplan 75K 75,000 Gold Aeroplan Super Elite 125,000 Gold Get up to 20,000 additional Status Qualifying Credits per year Beyond the automatic 5,000 SQCs you’ll receive each calendar year just for having the Air Canada Aeroplan Card, you can earn up to 20,000 additional credits by hitting spending thresholds. Here’s how that breaks down: Earn 10,000 additional SQCs after spending $25,000 on purchases on the card in a calendar year Earn 10,000 additional SQCs on top of that after spending $50,000 on purchases on the card in a calendar year So you can earn a total of 25,000 SQCs each calendar year through the Air Canada Aeroplan Card. Whether or not that’s worth it really depends on how much you fly Air Canada, and what the opportunity cost of your credit card spending is. Qualify for Aeroplan 35K status Those with the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card can get a one-tier status upgrade to Aeroplan 35K status when they spend $75,000 on the card in a calendar year. You’ll get status for the remainder of the calendar year you qualify and the entire following calendar year. If you ask me, the value here is really for someone who is actually loyal to Air Canada. Aeroplan 35K status gets you three complimentary checked bags on Air Canada flights (vs. just one with Aeroplan 25K), 10 eUpgrade credits, and a 3x elite points multiplier on eligible Air Canada or Star Alliance flight bookings, among other things. The Aeroplan Card could help you work toward a higher status level Aeroplan Credit Card benefits & credits The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers a variety of valuable benefits and credits, beyond the elite status perks covered above. Some of these benefits are offered just for being a cardmember, while others can be earned with spending. The perks are pretty comprehensive, and you’ll find almost everything you could want short of lounge access. So let’s go over those. Up to $100 in Air Canada statement credits The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers up to $100 in Air Canada statement credits when you make qualifying Air Canada purchases. The credits apply to paid airfare, taxes and fees on award flights, and inflight food and drinks, though onboard Wi-Fi is excluded. This breaks down as two credits of up to $50 each, one from January 1 through June 30 and one from July 1 through December 31. If you book cash fares on Air Canada twice a year, this is an easy way to put $100 back in your pocket, and this benefit alone can cover about half of the card’s annual fee. 15% off Air Canada award flights As an Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card holder, you can receive a 15% discount on the Aeroplan points required to book an award flight on Air Canada, Air Canada Express, or Air Canada Rouge. In practice, this also seems to work on partner award flights, as long as at least one segment is on Air Canada. The upside here can be absolutely huge, and it’s a great reason to have this card. First checked bag free on Air Canada The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers a free first checked bag on Air Canada flights for the primary cardmember and up to eight others traveling on the same itinerary. This applies to itineraries with Air Canada, Air Canada Rouge, or Air Canada Express. The value of that could add up pretty quickly. There’s no need to actually pay for the ticket with the card, as long as you’re the primary cardmember and have your Aeroplan number linked to the reservation. Global Entry, TSA PreCheck, or NEXUS credit Once every four years, the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers a credit that’s valid toward a membership with Global Entry, TSA PreCheck, or NEXUS , worth up to $120. These are all programs that can save travelers time at the airport, and potentially even at the border. I specifically love that the card also offers a NEXUS credit, since that’s historically something we haven’t seen card issuers offer. NEXUS is arguably the best of the three programs, since it gets you access to Global Entry, TSA PreCheck, and expedited immigration in Canada. Get a TSA PreCheck credit with the Aeroplan Card Carbon offset program for Air Canada redemptions Admittedly this is probably more interesting in theory than in practice, but I still like where Aeroplan is going with this. Those with the Air Canada Aeroplan Card will automatically have carbon offsets purchased for their flights when redeeming Aeroplan points for an Air Canada flight. World Elite Mastercard perks The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card is a World Elite Mastercard, which comes with certain perks , including a concierge service and presale tickets for eligible events. Valuable travel coverage (flights, rental cars, and more) While you’ll want to consult the cardmember agreement for full details, the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers a variety of travel protection when paying with the card, including the following: Trip cancellation & interruption insurance Baggage delay insurance Trip delay reimbursement Auto rental collision damage waiver Roadside assistance Get collision damage waiver coverage with the Aeroplan Card Aeroplan Credit Card “Pay Yourself Back” feature There’s another feature that you’ll find on the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card, which isn’t available on any other airline card. Specifically, the Aeroplan Credit Card offers a Pay Yourself Back feature , whereby cardmembers can apply their Aeroplan points toward travel purchases on any airline, hotel, or rental car, at the rate of 1.25 cents per point, up to 200,000 points per year. This is an incredibly innovative concept, and something that cardmembers may find to be valuable. So whether you want to redeem your points for a stay at a Four Seasons or a flight on JetBlue, the possibilities are endless. It’s also a reason to potentially think of the welcome bonus differently — the bonus points earned with the welcome offer can over time be redeemed toward any recent purchase or even toward the card’s annual fee. Redeem Aeroplan points indirectly for JetBlue Mint Priority reward vouchers with spending The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card also offers the ability to earn priority reward vouchers. Each can be used to get 50% off an eligible Aeroplan award ticket, and is valid for travel on Air Canada or a partner airline. You earn these vouchers at the following four annual spending thresholds: $100,000 $250,000 $500,000 $750,000 These can each be used in the same way, and the value depends on your status: Aeroplan Elite 25K and Elite 35K members can only use these for economy awards wholly within the United States and Canada Aeroplan Elite 50K members can use these for economy and premium economy awards within North America Aeroplan Elite 75K members can use these for economy and premium economy awards worldwide Aeroplan Super Elite members can use these for economy, premium economy, or business class awards worldwide As you can tell, the value here will depend on your status and travel patterns, but there’s potentially quite a bit of value to be had. Earn Aeroplan award discounts for spending on the Aeroplan Card The ultimate million dollar companion certificate While this is something that most people won’t be able to achieve, I love the concept behind this, and for some it might just be the best deal in travel. title: Orient Express Sailing Yachts Review: Corinthian’s Suites, Dining, Amenities, Service, And More
summary: I spent four nights on the Corinthian, Orient Express Sailing Yachts' first ship, and found the suites, food, and service exceptional, if very expensive. Here's my full review.
content: Want to book Orient Express Sailing Yachts? Orient Express Sailing Yachts voyages are best booked through Accor Preferred travel advisors. They can get you the best price, and also add a shipboard credit. Ford and his team are happy to help with any requests, and can be reached at ford@fordbtravel.com. Email Ford For the main event of my Orient Express adventure via Africa trip , Ford and I had the chance to spend four nights on the Corinthian , which is the first ship in Orient Express’ new cruising venture , known as Orient Express Sailing Yachts. Orient Express Sailing Yachts set sail in the summer of 2026, and with just 54 suites that can accommodate up to 110 guests, it really brings luxury cruising to a new level. It’s a fascinating time for the luxury cruising industry more broadly, given how competition has been heating up. I also recently reviewed Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection , and had a great experience , and reviewed Four Seasons Yachts , which is definitely more luxurious, but also has some growing pains . Lastly, I’ve compared all the experiences as well . While Orient Express Sailing Yachts is the highest priced cruising venture to date, I have to say, the experience really is unbelievably good, and at least you feel like you’re getting an amazing experience. I come into these kinds of trips with a critical eye, and I was just blown away by the ship’s design, the quality of the food and drinks, and the service. To me the ship felt like a step back in time (in terms of its classic elegance), while also being cutting edge modern. If you can swing this experience, I’d highly recommend it. Okay, enough of an intro, here comes my 8,500-word review (yikes, this is the longest review I’ve ever published of anything). Orient Express Sailing Yachts itinerary, pricing, and how to book Orient Express Sailing Yachts charges per suite (rather than per person, based on double occupancy), and you’ll find that journeys typically cost an average of $4,000-6,000 per cabin per night for a base suite. Make no mistake, this is the very top end of the cruise market, and at this point you’re paying safari prices for the experience. Let me also emphasize that rates go up from there, and Orient Express Sailing Yachts has some of the most insane suites you’ll find at sea, some of which can cost six figures per sailing. Currently, Orient Express offers cruises in Europe in summer, and in the Caribbean in winter, with transatlantic sailings in the spring and fall. For what it’s worth, you’ll find rate parity regardless of which booking channel you reserve through. So your best bet is to book through a travel advisor affiliated with Accor Preferred , because they can add perks to your journey . The size of the credit depends on the accommodation type booked, plus the length of the journey. Ford and his team are of course happy to help with these bookings, and can be reached at ford@fordbtravel.com. In the interest of full disclosure, Ford was invited on this Orient Express Sailing Yachts journey (due to the amount of volume he books), and I tagged along with him. All opinions expressed are my own, and I plan to review this exactly the same way I reviewed the two previous cruises (which we paid full price for). I haven’t been asked to write anything, and I have no incentive to be anything other than honest. If people are going to drop a ton of money on a luxury cruise, I want to make sure they’re at least getting the best experience possible. We experienced Orient Express Sailing Yachts in early October 2026, shortly before the ship’s transatlantic sailing. Admittedly it wasn’t the most exciting itinerary, but that’s just what worked out for us in terms of timing, since we wanted to minimize our time away from home, had to schedule it around when family could best be with our kids, etc. Below is the itinerary for the sailing we took. Date Port Arrival Departure Mon, October 5 Marseille, France – 7:00PM Tue, October 6 Mahón, Spain 1:00PM – Wed, October 7 Mahón, Spain – 5:00PM Thu, October 8 Day at sea – – Fri, October 9 Malaga, Spain 10:00AM – We were happy with this itinerary, since our primary goal was to see the ship. It definitely wasn’t the most exciting, though, given that we docked at the port in Mahón (rather than tendering), and it also meant we didn’t have a marina day (not that you’d necessarily want that in October, since it’s a bit chillier). But the point is that if you’re traveling more in peak season, you can expect a marina day more consistently. Orient Express Sailing Yachts inclusions Historically, cruising has been all about offering an all-inclusive experience. That’s true with Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection, but then Four Seasons Yachts countered the trend, by only including breakfast, and then charging extra for lunch, dinner, and drinks (I don’t love this concept, especially given the quality issues they have). While Orient Express Sailing Yachts might charge a lot, what I really appreciate is how the company has an ultra all-inclusive concept, to an extent that’s even greater than you’ll find on most other cruise lines. Orient Express Sailing Yachts journeys include the following: All-suite accommodations, including butler service for all guests Meals and drinks, including at bars and restaurants, as well as via 24-hour room service; only one specialty restaurant isn’t included, and there are also some premium drinks that cost extra (but the drinks included are really impressive) Entertainment and leisure, including live music, interactive programs, a recording studio, a kids club on select voyages, unlimited Starlink Wi-Fi, etc. Wellness and relaxation, including access to the spa, and instructor-led fitness classes and training Select excursions, with some inclusive shore activities Airport or hotel transfers on arrival and departure, with effortless check-in and personalized assistance before and during the journey Gratuities for staff Orient Express Sailing Yachts journeys don’t include the following: Select wine and spirits, dining at La Table (the fine dining restaurant), and treatments at the Guerlain Spa, barber shop, and beauty salon Optional shore excursions, beyond the ones that are included Flights, hotel stays, and rail arrangements Regarding the Orient Express Sailing Yachts tipping policy, the company states that gratuities are included in the fare — “however, if you wish to offer a tip as an extra gesture of appreciation, it will be warmly received.” I just have to emphasize that the level of inclusions really impressed me. Seriously, I was served caviar with breakfast, lunch, and dinner at various points (and even cocktails!), and the house champagne is Veuve Clicquot La Grande Dame 2018 (which retails for around $200 per bottle). Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian ship layout & basics Orient Express Sailing Yachts currently has a single ship, which is named the Corinthian (a second ship is being introduced in 2027, and it’ll be named the Olympian). The ship entered service in 2026, and is 722 feet (220 meters) long, 82 feet (25 meters) wide, and 26,600 gross tons. With 54 accommodations and a maximum capacity of around 110 guests, there’s a roughly 1.5:1 staff to guest ratio, given that there are around 170 staff onboard. The spaciousness of this ship, and the amount of space allocated to each passenger, really is next level. The Corinthian also has the title of being the world’s largest sailing yacht, as it has three automated SolidSail rigid sails on tilting carbon masts, to provide wind propulsion, alongside hybrid LNG auxiliary power. It’s just such an elegant and distinctive looking ship, that it can’t help but turn heads. For those curious, it was explained that the sails reduce emissions by around 10%, and no, the ship doesn’t “heel” in the way a smaller sailboat would. Unless you’re looking up, you wouldn’t realize there are even sails. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian exterior You can find the full Corinthian deck plan here . And let me just say, they’re also not cheap with the pours — you can barely go anywhere without having a glass pushed on you. 😉 Orient Express Sailing Yachts house champagne Of course there’s also a premium drink list with even more special wines and spirits, and those come at an extra cost. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian service I have to acknowledge that our sailing was rather empty, so the staff to guest ratio on this sailing was unreal. That being said, it wasn’t just the ratio that was amazing, but the quality of staff was really incredible as well. If you don’t have good staff, they’ll find a way to disappoint even if the staff to guest ratio is amazing. I’m not exaggerating when I say that service on Orient Express Sailing Yachts was flawless in terms of attention to detail, and that was such a contrast to our Four Seasons Yachts experience. It’s hard to even pinpoint any one area that impressed me, because it was just very consistent, polished, and proactive, across the board. Let me just give a few examples: Reuben was our assigned butler, and he was top notch; he was incredibly attentive without being overbearing, and every single request we had was taken care of in no time, with perfect precision I found it noteworthy that the staff on Orient Express Sailing Yachts seemed to be a mix of people with cruising experience, as well as a lot of people with more land-based hospitality experience, including many staff having worked in hospitality or fashion in France The attention to detail was excellent across the board — for example, our preferences were remembered each morning with breakfast, our water preferences were remembered at meals, and our dietary preferences and restrictions were also automatically factored in across venues Just to demonstrate attention to detail, Ford isn’t drinking right now, but the bartenders not only constantly recommended inventive mocktails, but they even made sure that the non-alcoholic drinks were stocked in whatever venue we were going to; for example, we told our butler we’d go to the bar one evening (per his recommendation, since we hadn’t been at that point), and as soon as we walked in, the bartender explained all the non-alcoholic options they had Service just felt very refined, old world, and formal, without being stuffy; for example, even the suite attendants change uniforms throughout the day, some of the staff wear white gloves at night, etc. On the first day I mentioned how I’d like a little milk in the minibar for my morning coffee (since it wasn’t otherwise stocked), and then it was always just automatically refilled, even though it wasn’t otherwise a standard part of the setup, which shows a focus on details As I said in my Four Seasons Yachts review, while we had an amazing time, we had way more service issues than I’d consider to be acceptable, given the price point. This was exactly the opposite, and it was just flawless service experience after flawless service experience. So while I’m sure service is consistently good, I’m sure the empty sailing also contributed to taking this to the next level. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian guest profile We were definitely on an odd sailing, in terms of seasonality, since we were on the second to last voyage before the ship sailed across the Atlantic, to start the winter season in the Caribbean. Our sailing was empty, with just 19 of the 54 suites occupied, so there were fewer than 40 guests. It really felt like having a private yacht, as we rarely saw others, and we’d go to restaurants for dinner, at most a handful of other tables would be occupied. On our sailing, almost everyone seemed to be a European retiree, so it was maybe in line with what you’d expect from the stereotypical guest profile of Orient Express trains. However, Ford has had some clients on Orient Express Sailing Yachts, and based on the feedback he has gotten, the ship can be an absolute scene, with some pretty over-the-top people. The guest profile that Orient Express Sailing Yachts gets is probably a bit different than almost any other cruise line. For one, the ship has already been chartered multiple times in its first season, so you can imagine the kinds of people we’re talking about. And even on sailings that haven’t been chartered, there have been some A-list people onboard. So anyway, we had a very pleasant, understated crowd onboard, but I’ve also heard the crowd can make for quite some people watching, especially for sailings in the South of France, etc. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian areas for improvement As I said at the beginning, my goal here is to be as objective as possible, so what feedback do I have? Honestly, as much as I have a critical eye, I think there are shockingly few areas for improvements. Here are the things that stood out to me: The butler service concept is really well executed, except I wish there were a way to message with the butler, rather than having to call them; it would just be so much more efficient, and would also be better if you have a request while on shore In some cases the two primary bars (Le Wagon Bar and Le Speakeasy) only open at 9:30PM or 10:30PM, which is mighty late; I get that these are supposed to have a late night vibe, but it would be nice if there were a more “happening” bar a little bit earlier It’s not really a problem, but the massive entertainment area seems really underutilized; I’m not sure what the solution is, since I think the demand for entertainment like that just isn’t there for a ship like this Obviously if you’re looking for a huge pool to splash around in, this ship probably isn’t for you, but that’s also not what they’re going for; as I already mentioned, I also wish there would be a hot tub I also want to acknowledge that Trek Trendy had published a review of the Orient Express Corinthian, and I think that’s worth watching for a different perspective. I think he was being totally fair with some of his critique, but I had a different experience: I think they took some of that feedback to heart, and the limited hours of some of the venues have been extended (particularly the library bar, and the bar on the top floor) It seems that technically they allow smoking by the pool, and I could see how that would be disruptive; nobody on my cruise was a smoker, best I could tell, so that wasn’t an issue for us It sounds like his sailing was also a bit busier, and might’ve had some “interesting” characters onboard, and I can see how that could change the experience a bit I agree with the general issue of some of the venues sometimes lacking a “vibe,” given that out of at most 110 guests, it might not be uncommon to just have the bars be totally empty late at night; however, I’ve heard that on other sailings, the bars are popping off, so I think it’s very journey and guest dependent Bottom line I travel a ton, and as much as I have so many amazing experiences, I’m almost always excited to go home, given that I miss family, and travel is sort of my “job.” I have to be honest, the Orient Express Corinthian was the first time in recent memory where I thought to myself “man, I wish it weren’t over.” Earlier this year I experienced Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection and Four Seasons Yachts, and they’re both great in their own ways. However, Orient Express Sailing Yachts is really in a different league. Yes, it’s priced at the top end of the market, but it also includes the most, and I really appreciate that. There’s something nice about paying a high voyage cost in advance, but then feeling like everything is included. Orient Express Sailing Yachts really is an unbelievable product, from the design of the ship, to the incredible restaurant and bar concepts, to the service. If you can swing it — and especially if you’ve never taken a cruise before — I can’t recommend this enough. What’s your take on the Orient Express cruise concept?

title: Orient Express Sailing Yachts Review: Corinthian’s Suites, Dining, Amenities, Service, And More
summary: I spent four nights on the Corinthian, Orient Express Sailing Yachts' first ship, and found the suites, food, and service exceptional, if very expensive. Here's my full review.
content: Want to book Orient Express Sailing Yachts? Orient Express Sailing Yachts voyages are best booked through Accor Preferred travel advisors. They can get you the best price, and also add a shipboard credit. Ford and his team are happy to help with any requests, and can be reached at ford@fordbtravel.com. Email Ford For the main event of my Orient Express adventure via Africa trip , Ford and I had the chance to spend four nights on the Corinthian , which is the first ship in Orient Express’ new cruising venture , known as Orient Express Sailing Yachts. Orient Express Sailing Yachts set sail in the summer of 2026, and with just 54 suites that can accommodate up to 110 guests, it really brings luxury cruising to a new level. It’s a fascinating time for the luxury cruising industry more broadly, given how competition has been heating up. I also recently reviewed Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection , and had a great experience , and reviewed Four Seasons Yachts , which is definitely more luxurious, but also has some growing pains . Lastly, I’ve compared all the experiences as well . While Orient Express Sailing Yachts is the highest priced cruising venture to date, I have to say, the experience really is unbelievably good, and at least you feel like you’re getting an amazing experience. I come into these kinds of trips with a critical eye, and I was just blown away by the ship’s design, the quality of the food and drinks, and the service. To me the ship felt like a step back in time (in terms of its classic elegance), while also being cutting edge modern. If you can swing this experience, I’d highly recommend it. Okay, enough of an intro, here comes my 8,500-word review (yikes, this is the longest review I’ve ever published of anything). Orient Express Sailing Yachts itinerary, pricing, and how to book Orient Express Sailing Yachts charges per suite (rather than per person, based on double occupancy), and you’ll find that journeys typically cost an average of $4,000-6,000 per cabin per night for a base suite. Make no mistake, this is the very top end of the cruise market, and at this point you’re paying safari prices for the experience. Let me also emphasize that rates go up from there, and Orient Express Sailing Yachts has some of the most insane suites you’ll find at sea, some of which can cost six figures per sailing. Currently, Orient Express offers cruises in Europe in summer, and in the Caribbean in winter, with transatlantic sailings in the spring and fall. For what it’s worth, you’ll find rate parity regardless of which booking channel you reserve through. So your best bet is to book through a travel advisor affiliated with Accor Preferred , because they can add perks to your journey . The size of the credit depends on the accommodation type booked, plus the length of the journey. Ford and his team are of course happy to help with these bookings, and can be reached at ford@fordbtravel.com. In the interest of full disclosure, Ford was invited on this Orient Express Sailing Yachts journey (due to the amount of volume he books), and I tagged along with him. All opinions expressed are my own, and I plan to review this exactly the same way I reviewed the two previous cruises (which we paid full price for). I haven’t been asked to write anything, and I have no incentive to be anything other than honest. If people are going to drop a ton of money on a luxury cruise, I want to make sure they’re at least getting the best experience possible. We experienced Orient Express Sailing Yachts in early October 2026, shortly before the ship’s transatlantic sailing. Admittedly it wasn’t the most exciting itinerary, but that’s just what worked out for us in terms of timing, since we wanted to minimize our time away from home, had to schedule it around when family could best be with our kids, etc. Below is the itinerary for the sailing we took. Date Port Arrival Departure Mon, October 5 Marseille, France – 7:00PM Tue, October 6 Mahón, Spain 1:00PM – Wed, October 7 Mahón, Spain – 5:00PM Thu, October 8 Day at sea – – Fri, October 9 Malaga, Spain 10:00AM – We were happy with this itinerary, since our primary goal was to see the ship. It definitely wasn’t the most exciting, though, given that we docked at the port in Mahón (rather than tendering), and it also meant we didn’t have a marina day (not that you’d necessarily want that in October, since it’s a bit chillier). But the point is that if you’re traveling more in peak season, you can expect a marina day more consistently. Orient Express Sailing Yachts inclusions Historically, cruising has been all about offering an all-inclusive experience. That’s true with Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection, but then Four Seasons Yachts countered the trend, by only including breakfast, and then charging extra for lunch, dinner, and drinks (I don’t love this concept, especially given the quality issues they have). While Orient Express Sailing Yachts might charge a lot, what I really appreciate is how the company has an ultra all-inclusive concept, to an extent that’s even greater than you’ll find on most other cruise lines. Orient Express Sailing Yachts journeys include the following: All-suite accommodations, including butler service for all guests Meals and drinks, including at bars and restaurants, as well as via 24-hour room service; only one specialty restaurant isn’t included, and there are also some premium drinks that cost extra (but the drinks included are really impressive) Entertainment and leisure, including live music, interactive programs, a recording studio, a kids club on select voyages, unlimited Starlink Wi-Fi, etc. Wellness and relaxation, including access to the spa, and instructor-led fitness classes and training Select excursions, with some inclusive shore activities Airport or hotel transfers on arrival and departure, with effortless check-in and personalized assistance before and during the journey Gratuities for staff Orient Express Sailing Yachts journeys don’t include the following: Select wine and spirits, dining at La Table (the fine dining restaurant), and treatments at the Guerlain Spa, barber shop, and beauty salon Optional shore excursions, beyond the ones that are included Flights, hotel stays, and rail arrangements Regarding the Orient Express Sailing Yachts tipping policy, the company states that gratuities are included in the fare — “however, if you wish to offer a tip as an extra gesture of appreciation, it will be warmly received.” I just have to emphasize that the level of inclusions really impressed me. Seriously, I was served caviar with breakfast, lunch, and dinner at various points (and even cocktails!), and the house champagne is Veuve Clicquot La Grande Dame 2018 (which retails for around $200 per bottle). Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian ship layout & basics Orient Express Sailing Yachts currently has a single ship, which is named the Corinthian (a second ship is being introduced in 2027, and it’ll be named the Olympian). The ship entered service in 2026, and is 722 feet (220 meters) long, 82 feet (25 meters) wide, and 26,600 gross tons. With 54 accommodations and a maximum capacity of around 110 guests, there’s a roughly 1.5:1 staff to guest ratio, given that there are around 170 staff onboard. The spaciousness of this ship, and the amount of space allocated to each passenger, really is next level. The Corinthian also has the title of being the world’s largest sailing yacht, as it has three automated SolidSail rigid sails on tilting carbon masts, to provide wind propulsion, alongside hybrid LNG auxiliary power. It’s just such an elegant and distinctive looking ship, that it can’t help but turn heads. For those curious, it was explained that the sails reduce emissions by around 10%, and no, the ship doesn’t “heel” in the way a smaller sailboat would. Unless you’re looking up, you wouldn’t realize there are even sails. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian exterior You can find the full Corinthian deck plan here . As you’d expect for a sail boat, there aren’t quite as many floors as on a traditional cruise ship. Guests can access a total of five floors, between levels three and seven. To briefly cover that: Level three is where you get on and off the ship, including via tenders Level four has reception, the wellness and entertainment areas, and some suites Level five has some of the restaurants, bars, and the pool, as well as some suites Level six has more restaurants, and some suites Level seven has some of the specialty suites, and it’s also where the top floor deck is located Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian directory Near the ship’s entrance, you’ll find a very cool directory of sorts, which shows the floorplan of the ship. You can click any amenity, and then it will light up, so that’s super handy. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian design Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian floorplan The ship has two sets of elevator banks, as well as two sets of staircases, so getting around the ship is really easy. We always used the stairs, since we were typically within a couple of floors of where we needed to be. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian staircase Orient Express Sailing Yachts check-in, boarding, & tendering As you’d expect, the ease of boarding a ship varies greatly depending on its size, but Orient Express Sailing Yachts really took it to the next level in terms of how seamless it was. We had spent a night at the Hôtel Dieu Intercontinental Marseille. Our journey included the transfers, so an Orient Express representative met us at the hotel, and then we were driven to the port. Orient Express Sailing Yachts included transfer Getting onboard the ship literally couldn’t have been easier. There were no formalities in the port, but instead, we were escorted straight through security, and then check-in was handled once onboard. There were no other guests as we boarded, and the staff really went above and beyond — for example, the crew member who escorted us through security and onto the ship insisted on holding an umbrella over our heads, to shade us from the sun. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian exterior Our check-in process onboard took all of five minutes, and at that point we were introduced to our butler, Reuben, who escorted us to our suite, and took care of everything from there. I should mention how Reuben was German, so they specifically appointed us a German butler, which I thought was super fun (so we communicated with him exclusively in German). We didn’t have a stop that involved tendering, but for those situations where you do, it’s an efficient process, given how few guests there are. Our one stop had us docked in port, and there was a nice seating area outside the ship with bottled water, sunscreen, etc. Admittedly a setup like this is more useful when you’re waiting on a tender, rather than just walking directly onto or off the ship. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian exterior Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suites Orient Express Sailing Yachts has 54 suites onboard, spread across over a dozen different categories. The entry level suites here are among the most spacious at sea, while the penthouse suites really take luxury and space to the next level. Our sailing was rather empty — only 19 of the 54 suites were occupied — and we were upgraded to a higher suite category (I believe they had blocked most of the entry level room categories, as they were doing some minor updates to them ahead of the ship heading to the Caribbean). So let me share my thoughts on that suite first, and then I’ll share some pictures of other suites that I had the opportunity to tour as well. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Appartement Prestige We stayed in an Appartement Prestige, which is one of the more premium standard suite categories, but below the duplex suites and penthouse suites. These suites are marketed as being an average of 1,119 square feet (104 square meters), so they’re incredibly spacious. We were assigned suite 518, located on the fifth floor. The hallways on the Corinthian are just stunning, as you can see below. It really feels more like a luxury hotel than a ship, especially in terms of the width of the hallway. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian hallway The concept of forgetting that one is on a ship continued inside the suite. The interior felt more to me like a “Palace” hotel in France , than what you’d expect at sea. I can’t even imagine how much money was spent on the interiors, as the quality of the finishes, from the wall treatments to the carpet, as well as the furniture, was just unreal. Upon entering the suite, there was first a dining area with a table and a chair, as well as a desk with a chair (that chair could also be moved over to the dining table). It’s not often you get this kind of space in a cruise ship suite. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite dining area Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite desk area The minibar was also in this area, and was well stocked, with everything being complimentary. This included a Nespresso coffee machine, cocktails, wine, beer, soft drinks, etc. They were also happy to replenish the minibar however you wanted, so there are really no limits. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite minibar Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite minibar Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite minibar That entry area then flowed into the living room, which was gorgeous. It had a couch and a coffee table, as well as a hidden TV (which would pop up from in front of the mirror). Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite living room Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite living room Waiting on the dining table was a lovely welcome amenity, consisting of some freshly baked treats, a fruit plate, and a bottle of Veuve Clicquot 2015 Rose. There was also an Orient Express branded journal, along with two Orient Express water bottles, which guests could take home. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian welcome amenity Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian welcome amenity Double doors then led into the bedroom, which had a very plush king size bed. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite bedroom Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite bedroom Much like with the bedroom, the bathroom will make you forget that you’re on a ship, as it had double sinks, a soaking tub, a walk-in shower with amazing water pressure, and a toilet in a separate room. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite bathroom Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite bathtub Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite shower Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite toilet There were also a couple of closet areas, so there was plenty of space to store luggage and clothes. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite closet The suite then had a balcony that stretched the entire length of the suite, with very comfortable furniture. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite balcony Beyond the generally beautiful design, it has to be pointed out just how over the top everything was. I mean, the deck furniture uses fabrics from Loro Piana, just to give you a sense of just how high-end it is. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian Loro Piana furniture fabric Housekeeping in the room was great (it was taken care of twice daily, and always well timed), butler service was very useful (more on that a bit later, when I talk about service), Starlink Wi-Fi was lightning fast, and I also love how Orient Express Sailing Yachts includes laundry. You could get unlimited washing, dry cleaning, etc., so that’s a very nice feature. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian complimentary laundry Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian complimentary laundry Orient Express Sailing Yachts Suite Panoramique In the interest of checking out different suite products, I also had the chance to tour the Suite Panoramique, which is the entry level accommodation onboard, located on levels four and five. These are 506 square feet (47 square meters), so they’re spacious for an entry level suite on a cruise. This had the same general design concept as the suite we were in, except there wasn’t a fully separate living area. The suite had a comfortable king size bed, a desk with a chair, a dining table, and a huge window with a double daybed of sorts. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite bed Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite desk area While there was no bathtub, the bathroom still had double sinks, a walk-in shower, and a toilet in a separate room. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite bathroom Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite toilet Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite shower To point out the obvious, these entry level suites don’t have balconies. Of course people prefer to have balconies, but this is just a simple reality of the difference between sailboats and cruise ships, in terms of how many levels there are, how far above water they are, etc. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Zephyr Suite Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ top end suites are really next level, so I also had the chance to tour the Zephyr Suite, which is located on level seven, and is the second most premium suite onboard. This two bedroom suite has 2,486 square feet (231 square meters) of interior space, plus a terrace that’s 1,206 square feet (112 square meters). What I thought was so cool was how unique the design of this suite was, as the top suite products seem to have a totally original design. This very much had a residential vibe, with a long hallway connecting the various parts of the suite. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite hallway Seriously, check out this living room… Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite living room Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite living room …and the two bedrooms… Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite bedroom Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite bedroom …and the TV room… Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite TV room …and the bathrooms… Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite bathroom Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite bathroom …and the massive terrace. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite terrace Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite terrace However, perhaps the coolest feature was the replica of an Orient Express Heritage cabin, intended to pay homage to the legendary train. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian suite replica train cabin Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian pools & decks The Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian has two pools onboard, with one being rather traditional, and one being unlike anything else at sea (at least to my knowledge). The main “leisure” pool is located on the fifth floor, at the back of the ship. While the pool has beautiful aesthetics and lovely deck space around it, this isn’t some destination pool in and of itself.
