Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian guest profile We were definitely on an odd sailing, in terms of seasonality, since we were on the second to last voyage before the ship sailed across the Atlantic, to start the winter season in the Caribbean. Our sailing was empty, with just 19 of the 54 suites occupied, so there were fewer than 40 guests. It really felt like having a private yacht, as we rarely saw others, and we’d go to restaurants for dinner, at most a handful of other tables would be occupied. On our sailing, almost everyone seemed to be a European retiree, so it was maybe in line with what you’d expect from the stereotypical guest profile of Orient Express trains. However, Ford has had some clients on Orient Express Sailing Yachts, and based on the feedback he has gotten, the ship can be an absolute scene, with some pretty over-the-top people. The guest profile that Orient Express Sailing Yachts gets is probably a bit different than almost any other cruise line. For one, the ship has already been chartered multiple times in its first season, so you can imagine the kinds of people we’re talking about. And even on sailings that haven’t been chartered, there have been some A-list people onboard. So anyway, we had a very pleasant, understated crowd onboard, but I’ve also heard the crowd can make for quite some people watching, especially for sailings in the South of France, etc. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian areas for improvement As I said at the beginning, my goal here is to be as objective as possible, so what feedback do I have? Honestly, as much as I have a critical eye, I think there are shockingly few areas for improvements. Here are the things that stood out to me: The butler service concept is really well executed, except I wish there were a way to message with the butler, rather than having to call them; it would just be so much more efficient, and would also be better if you have a request while on shore In some cases the two primary bars (Le Wagon Bar and Le Speakeasy) only open at 9:30PM or 10:30PM, which is mighty late; I get that these are supposed to have a late night vibe, but it would be nice if there were a more “happening” bar a little bit earlier It’s not really a problem, but the massive entertainment area seems really underutilized; I’m not sure what the solution is, since I think the demand for entertainment like that just isn’t there for a ship like this Obviously if you’re looking for a huge pool to splash around in, this ship probably isn’t for you, but that’s also not what they’re going for; as I already mentioned, I also wish there would be a hot tub I also want to acknowledge that Trek Trendy had published a review of the Orient Express Corinthian, and I think that’s worth watching for a different perspective. I think he was being totally fair with some of his critique, but I had a different experience: I think they took some of that feedback to heart, and the limited hours of some of the venues have been extended (particularly the library bar, and the bar on the top floor) It seems that technically they allow smoking by the pool, and I could see how that would be disruptive; nobody on my cruise was a smoker, best I could tell, so that wasn’t an issue for us It sounds like his sailing was also a bit busier, and might’ve had some “interesting” characters onboard, and I can see how that could change the experience a bit I agree with the general issue of some of the venues sometimes lacking a “vibe,” given that out of at most 110 guests, it might not be uncommon to just have the bars be totally empty late at night; however, I’ve heard that on other sailings, the bars are popping off, so I think it’s very journey and guest dependent Bottom line I travel a ton, and as much as I have so many amazing experiences, I’m almost always excited to go home, given that I miss family, and travel is sort of my “job.” I have to be honest, the Orient Express Corinthian was the first time in recent memory where I thought to myself “man, I wish it weren’t over.” Earlier this year I experienced Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection and Four Seasons Yachts, and they’re both great in their own ways. However, Orient Express Sailing Yachts is really in a different league. Yes, it’s priced at the top end of the market, but it also includes the most, and I really appreciate that. There’s something nice about paying a high voyage cost in advance, but then feeling like everything is included. Orient Express Sailing Yachts really is an unbelievable product, from the design of the ship, to the incredible restaurant and bar concepts, to the service. If you can swing it — and especially if you’ve never taken a cruise before — I can’t recommend this enough. What’s your take on the Orient Express cruise concept?
